items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: In the days of the kings, queens, King Arthur, the roundtable, they had the court jester, that’s what he did, he rapped.

ctx.x: I object most to being yelled at by the music. I see these guys back and forth on the stage like yelling. It bothers me. What are you so mad about?

There is nothing new about rap. They acknowledge it as music now. This is music. But there’s nothing new about that. In the days of the kings, queens, King Arthur, the roundtable, they had the court jester, that’s what he did, he rapped. Nobody sang the songs, a melodic song. That’s all they did was rap. Then when I was a kid, a young dude, we had a thing we called “playing the dozens,” that was rapping. The dirty dozens you know, when you talked about each other’s mother and things like that. That was rap.…
Yeah it is unbelievable. Too many toys to play with I think.
